objective: Find the pairing behind the even counts of closed walks at FLIP-RULE-20261109-001B's six-contact example, prove the pairings found and an exact criterion for persistence without a flip, and classify the persistent contacts of the small maps by mechanism (exhaustive to six contacts, sampled to ten), stopping at a pairing or at none found.
status: Proved 2026-11-09: a contact persists exactly when deleting it keeps det(I + tN) over GF(2) (N the contact graph mod 2), i.e. when the cycle families through it are even in number at every size; doubled pairs (both darts of a contact leading to one contact) and automorphisms of the contact graph fixing it and exchanging its arcs pair its closed walks; FLIP-RULE-20261109-001B's six-contact example persists by two doubled pairs. Computed: on non-degenerate maps to six contacts every persistent contact that sends and hears is explained by a flip, a doubled pair or a contact-graph flip; from seven contacts most are explained by none (5,438 of 8,992 sampled at seven).
title: Why the parity comes out even
